inspection_summary: Inspected all 4,249 logical lines from front matter through references. The article supplies a connected semantic program: encode moment problems in several-variable Dirichlet series; use correction factors and functional-equation groups to expose polar divisors; derive conjectural general moment constants from orbit geometry; and, in the cubic quadratic case, prove continuation, sieve back to fundamental discriminants, and extract weighted and unweighted asymptotics. Prose is coherent throughout, but many displayed formulas are text-layer damaged, so exact formulas and constants in accepted spans remain scan-dependent.

sections_inspected.label: Front matter and abstract
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: States the several-variable continuation/polar-divisor program and the cubic application.

sections_inspected.label: 1. Introduction
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Defines multiple and perfect Dirichlet series, explains the moment bridge, finite-versus-infinite functional-equation boundary, main theorem, and conjectural higher-moment program.

sections_inspected.label: Moments of the Riemann zeta-function: background
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Separates arithmetic and geometric moment factors and relates random-matrix constants to a pole of a multiple Dirichlet series.

sections_inspected.label: 2.1. Multiple Dirichlet series for zeta
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Constructs the integral series, continues it past absolute convergence, identifies its w=1 residue, and factors that residue arithmetically.

sections_inspected.label: 2.2. Quasi-functional equations
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Defines the affine involution group and the stabilizer that reflects the initial polar hyperplane.

sections_inspected.label: 2.3. Fundamental conjecture for zeta
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Posits the required continuation and polar divisor, then converts the orbit sum into the zeta-moment leading constant via a Tauberian argument.

sections_inspected.label: 3. Quadratic Dirichlet moment background
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Records known moments and the symmetry-family conjecture for all positive integral moments.

sections_inspected.label: 3.1. Multiple Dirichlet series for the quadratic family
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Builds completed congruence-split series, proves functional equations, detects the w=1 residue by reciprocity, and recovers the arithmetic factor.

sections_inspected.label: 3.2. Fundamental conjecture for the quadratic family
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Formulates the polar-hyperplane continuation conjecture and evaluates the group-orbit singularity producing the geometric factor.

sections_inspected.label: 4 and 4.1. Cubic moments and foundations
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Specializes to the GL(3) Eisenstein realization and characterizes correction polynomials for imprimitive twists.

sections_inspected.label: 4.2. Cubic moment building blocks
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Packages corrected double Dirichlet series into vectors and derives functional equations in each variable.

sections_inspected.label: 4.3. Analytic continuation
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Uses tube domains, convex hulls, and a dihedral functional-equation group to continue the corrected series to C^2 after explicit polar cancellation.

sections_inspected.label: 4.4. Vertical-strip estimate
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Establishes finite order, transfers bounds through functional equations, and rules out spurious poles while retaining the reflected w=3/4 possibility.

sections_inspected.label: 4.5. Sieving process
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Möbius-sieves correction variables, reconstructs the fundamental-discriminant series, computes its leading pole, and derives the smoothed cubic asymptotic.

sections_inspected.label: 4.6. Unweighted estimate
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Combines short-interval moment bounds, truncated Perron integrals, oscillation, and parameter balancing to obtain the sharp-sum error exponent.

accepted_units.title: Perfect multiple Dirichlet series turn family averages into polar data
accepted_units.why_material: The source defines nested multiple Dirichlet series, explains how continuation in the averaging variable converts a pole into mean-value information, and motivates correction factors that reveal hidden functional equations after changing summation order.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the basic quadratic-twist example and the contrast with one-variable Rankin-Selberg continuation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low-to-moderate: the mechanism is explicit in prose; the displayed defining series is OCR-damaged and should be scan-checked for exact notation.

accepted_units.title: Finite functional-equation groups coincide with continuation and local uniqueness
accepted_units.why_material: For degrees one through three, reflected convergence regions have convex hull C^2 and local correction factors are uniquely forced; at degree four and above the group becomes infinite, uniqueness fails, and an essential-singularity boundary appears.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the article's central phase transition and later explains why the cubic family is the last completely tractable case.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low: the comparison and obstruction are prose-recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Cubic moment theorem and the higher-moment continuation gap
accepted_units.why_material: The main cubic asymptotics are paired with a diagnosis of the higher-moment barrier: many corrected series satisfy the same functional equations, yet the desired central point lies beyond the region generated from absolute convergence and before the expected essential-singularity curve.
accepted_units.context_note: Carries the first v1 span while retaining the surrounding finite/infinite-group context and the distinction between proved m=3 results and the m>=4 obstruction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: prose fixes the theorem's role and obstruction; exact coefficients and exponents require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Polar divisors provide a non-Euler-product route to zeta moments
accepted_units.why_material: The source proposes calculating all polar divisors through the central point, applies the program to an integral of shifted zeta factors, and stresses that functional equations plus continuation—not an Euler product—are the essential inputs.
accepted_units.context_note: Also contrasts the method with Good's integral series and approximate-functional-equation heuristics.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: the conceptual route is prose-clear; exact integral and domain boundaries are formula-dependent.

accepted_units.title: Arithmetic and geometric factors meet at a multiple-series pole
accepted_units.why_material: The historical moment problem is reframed by separating an Euler-product arithmetic factor from a random-matrix geometric factor and asserting that both occur in the residue structure at w=1.
accepted_units.context_note: Provides the target constants and the criterion that continuation slightly beyond the polar divisor would prove the moment conjecture.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: factor roles are prose-recoverable, while product formulas and normalization constants need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: An oscillatory integral family isolates the unique w=1 pole
accepted_units.why_material: The generalized integral series includes an oscillatory phase naturally produced by Stirling's formula; Proposition 2.1 gives initial continuation and singles out the zero-frequency case as the source of the simple w=1 pole.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the clean construction statement before the kernel estimates used in its proof.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate-to-high: prose identifies phase, domain, and pole, but exact inequalities and residue formula require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Oscillation continues Mellin kernels while zero frequency retains the pole
accepted_units.why_material: A model kernel is continued by integration by parts; nonzero logarithmic frequency gains holomorphy for Re(w)>0, whereas frequency zero and ratio one produce exactly the w=1 pole. Expanding zeta factors then transfers this dichotomy to the multiple series.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the residue/nonresidue split that operationalizes the pole-selection mechanism.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the integration-by-parts formulas are damaged, but the dichotomy, bounds, and application are recoverable from prose; scan-check exact expressions.

accepted_units.title: Near-diagonal multiplicative ratios are controlled by logarithmic separation
accepted_units.why_material: The proof handles the delicate nonresonant sum by splitting product ratios near and far from one and converting logarithmic denominators into divisor-sum estimates, completing continuation in the full stated si-region.
accepted_units.context_note: Retained because it explains why excluding the exact resonant diagonal suffices analytically rather than merely asserting convergence.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the summation formulas are OCR-fragmented; only the prose-supported decomposition and conclusion are reliable without a scan.

accepted_units.title: The w=1 residue factors into zeta diagonals and an arithmetic Euler product
accepted_units.why_material: The resonant condition is expressed multiplicatively, factored prime by prime, and separated into universal zeta singularities and a holomorphic remainder whose central specialization is the arithmetic moment factor.
accepted_units.context_note: Connects the analytic pole of the integral series to the conjectured arithmetic constant.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: factorization logic is prose-clear; exact Euler factors and indexing require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Quasi-functional involutions reflect the initial polar hyperplane
accepted_units.why_material: Affine involutions simultaneously reflect a zeta variable, shift w, flip a sign, and alter frequency. Their finite abelian group yields quasi-functional equations, while the frequency-zero stabilizer identifies precisely which reflections transport the w=1 pole.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the Stirling-tail reason the equations are quasi rather than exact and the subgroup generated by opposite-sign pairs.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate-to-high: transformations are visible but symbol-heavy and should be scan-checked exactly.

accepted_units.title: A polar-orbit continuation conjecture is sufficient for all even zeta moments
accepted_units.why_material: The conjecture specifies continuation to a tube containing the central point, no additional local polar components beyond the reflected w=1 hyperplane, and boundary holomorphy; a Tauberian theorem then reduces the moment conjecture to the leading Laurent coefficient.
accepted_units.context_note: Clearly separates the conjectural analytic input from the formal implication to moments.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: conjecture and implication are prose-clear; hyperplane equations and normalization require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Group symmetrization cancels lower Taylor data and selects the geometric constant
accepted_units.why_material: Summing a model principal part over the reflection group produces divisibility cancellations that make the central limit exist; positive-degree Taylor terms vanish after scaling, leaving the constant term and the random-matrix geometric factor.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the combinatorial engine converting the polar arrangement into the moment's geometric coefficient.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the invariant numerator/denominator argument is prose-recoverable, but exact products, group order, and limit normalization need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Quadratic-family symmetry predicts a different pole order and geometric factor
accepted_units.why_material: Known first through third moments and a conjectured fourth are organized into the general symplectic-family moment law, with pole degree m(m+1)/2 and a family-specific arithmetic factor.
accepted_units.context_note: Establishes the target that the subsequent quadratic multiple-series construction must recover.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: the progression and symmetry claim are prose-clear; exact constants and formulas need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Quadratic moment series expose the m>=4 shortage of usable functional equations
accepted_units.why_material: The fundamental-discriminant series directly encodes products of quadratic L-values, but the known continuation proof breaks at m>=4 because its functional equations do not reach beyond the first significant polar divisor near the central point.
accepted_units.context_note: Also records that the residue at w=1 already matches the conjectural constant, motivating the stronger continuation conjecture.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low-to-moderate: the obstruction and residue role are prose-recoverable; the defining series is formula-dependent.

accepted_units.title: Congruence splitting and gamma completion convert the raw family series into a finite-group invariant
accepted_units.why_material: The raw discriminant sum is split by sign and residue class, then completed by gamma factors so each coordinate functional equation becomes an affine involution and the resulting pair of series is invariant under a finite abelian group.
accepted_units.context_note: This representation change makes the polar orbit accessible while preserving the underlying family average.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the construction is readable in prose, but signs, congruence factors, and gamma normalizations require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Quadratic reciprocity makes square products the sole contributors to the w=1 residue
accepted_units.why_material: After expanding the L-functions and imposing squarefreeness, reciprocity rewrites the inner discriminant sum as ordinary character series. Only the principal-character case—equivalently a square product of indices—has a w=1 pole.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the elementary squarefree character-series lemma and recombination of residue classes.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the logical selection rule is prose-supported; exact local factors and residue formulas are OCR-damaged and need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Euler-product separation recovers the quadratic-family arithmetic factor
accepted_units.why_material: The square-product residue is factored into singular zeta factors and a holomorphic Euler product, then specialized at the center to identify exactly the arithmetic constant in the family moment conjecture.
accepted_units.context_note: Completes the arithmetic half of the conjectural moment coefficient before orbit geometry supplies the geometric half.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the factorization narrative is clear, but exact Euler products and central values require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: All reflected hyperplanes through the central point are posited as the local polar divisor
accepted_units.why_material: Finite-group invariance forces a family of 2^m candidate polar hyperplanes; Conjecture 3.6 asserts these are exactly the local divisor and that no w>1 obstruction remains, which is sufficient by a Tauberian theorem for even family moments.
accepted_units.context_note: Separates the analytic continuation assumption from the downstream asymptotic consequence.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: the conjecture is prose-clear; exact hyperplanes and constants need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Divisibility cancellation evaluates the quadratic-family geometric factor
accepted_units.why_material: The reflection-orbit sum is rewritten with a common denominator; symmetry and invariance force the numerator to contain all apparent singular factors, proving the central limit exists and reducing it to the constant Taylor term, which yields the geometric coefficient.
accepted_units.context_note: Quadratic-family analogue of the zeta orbit calculation, with a different hyperplane arrangement and factor.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the divisibility mechanism is recoverable from prose; exact products and normalization require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: The cubic family is realized as a GL(3) Eisenstein twist with imprimitive completions
accepted_units.why_material: The cube of a quadratic L-function is realized as a twisted GL(3) Eisenstein L-series. For nonsquarefree parameters, a Dirichlet polynomial repairs the twist so it obeys the same functional equation as a primitive character.
accepted_units.context_note: Explains why the degree-three case admits an exact corrected double-series construction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: realization and repair mechanism are prose-clear; local Euler and gamma factors need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Functional equations, squarefree invariance, and interchange determine local correction polynomials
accepted_units.why_material: Three functional identities plus a summation-interchange law characterize the P and Q correction polynomials uniquely in degrees one through three; simultaneous loss of uniqueness and finiteness at degree four explains the structural boundary.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the coefficient bound needed later to sum over imprimitive parameters and continue the series.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the four properties are symbol-heavy and require scan verification, while their uniqueness role is explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Reciprocity closes the w-functional equation on a finite character vector
accepted_units.why_material: The corrected building blocks are indexed by finitely many bad-prime characters. Interchanging summation, applying the character functional equation, and sieving residue classes expresses w reflection as a meromorphic matrix acting on this finite vector.
accepted_units.context_note: Finite-place two changes coefficients but not the closure mechanism.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: matrix closure is prose-supported; exact entries, gamma ratios, and character indices need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: The s-functional equation also closes after bad-prime bookkeeping
accepted_units.why_material: Applying the GL(3) twist functional equation and expanding omitted Euler factors yields a second finite-dimensional matrix relation reflecting s and shifting w. Together the two vector equations generate the continuation machinery.
accepted_units.context_note: The long scalar expansion demonstrates why vector packaging is the natural compression.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: exact scalar formula is heavily notation-dependent and must be scan-checked; the matrix-level relation is prose-recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Two involutions generate a dihedral group whose region hulls fill C^2
accepted_units.why_material: Tube-domain convexity converts overlapping analytic regions into their convex hulls. The two functional-equation involutions generate D12, and the staged hulls R1 to R2 to R3 to C^2 give a geometric continuation plan.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the cleanest source-level bridge from algebraic reflection data to global several-variable continuation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: definitions and staged hull claim are prose-clear; polygon coordinates and figures should be scan-checked.

accepted_units.title: Alternating reflections and polar cancellation produce an entire corrected series
accepted_units.why_material: Initial convergence estimates from both summation orders overlap to give R1; applying s, w, then s reflections and repeatedly taking tube convex hulls extends an explicitly pole-cancelled product to all C^2.
accepted_units.context_note: The proof also uses trivial L-function zeros to cancel apparent matrix-coefficient poles and removes one redundant linear factor.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the staged mechanism is prose-clear; the complete polar polynomial and finite Euler products need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Several-variable holomorphy converts boundary polynomial bounds into finite order
accepted_units.why_material: Vector functional equations transfer polynomial bounds around a reflected annular tube; a domain-of-holomorphy argument fills the central hole, proving the specialized entire function has order one.
accepted_units.context_note: Shows why a seemingly one-variable vertical-growth question still requires several-variable geometry.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate-to-high: the argument is prose-recoverable, but matrix products and figure-defined regions require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Mean-value input and reflection chains bound the corrected series across the critical strip
accepted_units.why_material: A fourth-moment estimate for quadratic twists yields absolute convergence on one boundary, while Proposition 4.12 states the reflected vertical-strip bound and limits possible poles to w=1 and w=3/4.
accepted_units.context_note: Supplies the analytic-growth interface needed for later contour shifts and sieving.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: qualitative bounds and pole locations are readable; exact exponents and sums require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Reflection paths eliminate spurious bad-prime poles but preserve a structural w=3/4 candidate
accepted_units.why_material: Alternating the two functional equations moves a difficult boundary point into absolute convergence and yields a convexity bound. Analyticity in two variables then rules out apparent poles from finite Euler factors by approaching along reflected hyperplanes; the orbit of w=1 leaves w=3/4 as a genuine possible pole.
accepted_units.context_note: Distinguishes artifacts of denominator clearing from polar loci permitted by the functional-equation geometry.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: reflection sequence and exact estimates are formula-dependent and need scan verification; the pole-elimination logic is prose-clear.

accepted_units.title: Möbius inversion turns corrected building blocks into the fundamental-discriminant series
accepted_units.why_material: Auxiliary divisibility parameters are introduced so Möbius summation forces the square multiplier to one. The target cubic moment series thereby inherits analytic continuation and vertical growth from the corrected Z_M family.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the target theorem: continuation past w=4/5, a seventh-order pole at one, and its leading coefficient.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the sieve principle and theorem are prose-recoverable; exact character-indexed series and leading constant need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Finite linear combinations restore bad Euler factors and isolate all fundamental-discriminant classes
accepted_units.why_material: Each divisibility-sieved series is expressed as a finite combination of previously continued Z_M blocks; a second Möbius sum removes imprimitive terms, and sign/congruence linear combinations reconstruct the full family while retaining the desired bounds.
accepted_units.context_note: Explains how a theorem for corrected all-integer sums becomes a theorem for the original arithmetic family.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: exact linear combination and exponents require scan verification; the two-stage sieve and congruence isolation are prose-clear.

accepted_units.title: Shifted continuation imports the general residue calculation and a Mellin shift yields the smoothed asymptotic
accepted_units.why_material: Rather than recompute a seventh-order residue, the cubic construction is extended to nearby shifted Eisenstein parameters and matched to the general Section 3 calculation. A Mellin inversion and contour shift then turn the pole at one into the full logarithmic polynomial with a power-saving error.
accepted_units.context_note: Separates residue identification from contour extraction and records why the weighted theorem attains the method's optimal error.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the argument is prose-clear; shifted local parameters, leading coefficient, and contour exponent require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: An unweighted signed sum requires a separate short-interval moment estimate
accepted_units.why_material: Removing smoothing cannot rely on positivity of cubic central values, so the proof imports a short-interval second-moment bound obtained from a degree-two corrected double series with nonnegative coefficients.
accepted_units.context_note: Identifies the genuinely new input needed to pass from the weighted to unweighted theorem.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: the strategic necessity and proof source are prose-clear; the precise exponent and range require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Short intervals control the truncation error by combining fourth and second moments
accepted_units.why_material: A truncated Perron integral approximates divisibility-restricted partial sums. The near-cutoff error is partitioned into short intervals and bounded by Cauchy-Schwarz using fourth-moment and short-interval second-moment estimates, while far terms use absolute convergence.
accepted_units.context_note: Gives the first quantitative bridge from the analytic series to a sharp cutoff.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: decomposition logic is prose-supported; exact interval parameters and error exponents require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: The functional equation converts the left contour into an oscillatory integral with a square-root saving
accepted_units.why_material: After contour shifting, a possible reflected-pole residue and three contour integrals appear. Reflecting the left edge into absolute convergence yields gamma-ratio phases; a second-derivative estimate saves a half-power of the height parameter.
accepted_units.context_note: This oscillatory saving is essential to the final unweighted exponent rather than routine contour bookkeeping.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the contour architecture is clear, but gamma products, phase, and exact powers require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: A divisor-sum lemma and parameter equalization determine the final error exponent
accepted_units.why_material: A dyadic divisor-sum bound feeds all contour and truncation errors; splitting small and large sieve moduli, choosing distinct heights, and equalizing the four dominant powers yields the stated unweighted error exponent.
accepted_units.context_note: Shows the exponent is the solution of a constrained balance, not an isolated estimate.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the optimization narrative is prose-recoverable; inequalities, parameter values, and radical exponent require scan verification.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: From a polar orbit to a zeta-moment constant
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The residue Euler product supplies the arithmetic factor, while the reflected polar arrangement and orbit cancellation supply pole order and the geometric factor; Tauberian transfer then yields the moment asymptotic.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The conclusion is conditional on the continuation and exact local-polar-divisor assertions of Conjecture 2.7.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: The finite/infinite functional-equation boundary
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: In this source, finiteness of the reflection group aligns both with uniqueness of local correction data and with a convex-hull route to the needed continuation, whereas degree four and above lose both properties.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The alignment is a source-supported structural diagnosis, not a proof that group infinitude alone causes every higher-moment obstruction.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Quadratic-family residue pipeline
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Congruence splitting and completion create a finite reflection action; reciprocity selects square products for the initial residue; Euler factorization produces the arithmetic constant; and orbit evaluation produces the geometric constant.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The final all-m implication remains conditional on Conjecture 3.6 and the theorem is stated for even moments in the Tauberian step.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Cubic proof architecture from correction to moment

within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This pipeline is specialized to the degree-three Eisenstein realization, and exact formula-level reuse requires scan verification because of OCR damage.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: The cost of removing smoothing

within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The resulting exponent is conditional on the specific mean-value inputs and bounds used here and is not presented as an intrinsic barrier.
